title: Flight into the wilderness
summary: Warned by the Lord, Alma's people gather their flocks and grain and leave before Noah's armies. They flee eight days into the wilderness, and the armies cannot overtake them.

explicit_facts.text: Alma warns his people that Noah's armies are coming; they gather flocks and grain and depart into the wilderness before the armies.
The people of king Noah cannot overtake Alma's people to destroy them.
They flee eight days' journey into the wilderness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people travel with their flocks and gathered grain.
unspecified_visual_details: The Lord's appearance, if any.
The people's clothing, ages, and exact number.
The landscape and weather.

narration.text: they fled eight days’ journey into the wilderness.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage attributes their escape to the Lord's strengthening; it does not describe a visible miracle.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting the Lord visibly or showing a supernatural intervention not described in the verses.

title: A land for settlement
summary: They arrive at a beautiful, pleasant land with pure water, pitch tents, till the ground, and begin building.

explicit_facts.text: They come to a very beautiful and pleasant land with pure water.
They pitch tents, till the ground, and begin building; they are industrious and work exceedingly.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Tents, cultivated ground, and buildings in progress are visible.
unspecified_visual_details: The land's precise geography, plants, and colors.
The design of the tents and buildings.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The land is later called Helam.
prohibited_inventions: Adding a specific water source, crop, or building design not stated in the passage.

title: The people ask Alma to be king
summary: The people want Alma as their king because they love him. Alma teaches against esteeming one person above another and says having a king would be well if they could always have just kings.

explicit_facts.text: The people desire Alma as king because he is beloved by them.
Alma says it is not expedient to have a king and teaches that one person should not be esteemed above another.
Alma says having a king would be well if they could always have just men as kings.

unspecified_visual_details: Whether the gathering is inside or outdoors.
The people's gestures and arrangement.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, it is not expedient that we should have a king;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma

spoken_dialogue.text: Ye shall not esteem one flesh above another,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma

spoken_dialogue.text: if it were possible that ye could always have just men to be your kings it would be well for you to have a king.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Alma's teaching about kings is conditional, not a claim that all kings are unjust.
prohibited_inventions: Showing a coronation or an actual king.

title: Alma recalls his repentance
summary: Alma reminds the people of Noah and his priests' iniquity, his own past wrongdoing and repentance, and the Lord's answer to his prayers. He says he does not glory in himself.

explicit_facts.text: Alma recalls king Noah and his priests' iniquity and says he was caught in a snare, did abominable things, and repented sorely.
After tribulation, the Lord hears and answers Alma's prayers and makes him an instrument in bringing many to knowledge of the Lord's truth.
Alma says he is unworthy to glory of himself.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma continues addressing the people; the past events are recounted rather than shown as occurring now.
unspecified_visual_details: The specific past actions Alma refers to.
Any visible form or appearance of the Lord.

spoken_dialogue.text: I myself was caught in a snare, and did many things which were abominable in the sight of the Lord,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma

spoken_dialogue.text: I do not glory, for I am unworthy to glory of myself.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Alma's account of earlier events should remain off-screen; no specific past deeds are identified here.
prohibited_inventions: Flashbacks depicting unspecified wrongdoing or a visible Lord.

title: Stand fast in liberty
summary: Alma says the people were oppressed and brought into iniquity by Noah and his priests, but delivered from bondage. He urges them to stand fast in liberty and trust only a godly teacher or minister.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says the people were oppressed and in bondage to Noah and his priests, who brought them into iniquity.
Alma says God delivered them from Noah's people and from the bonds of iniquity, and urges them to stand fast in liberty and not trust a man as king.
Alma says not to trust a teacher or minister unless the person is of God, walks in God's ways, and keeps his commandments.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma teaches the people in their settlement.
unspecified_visual_details: Any physical representation of bondage or deliverance.

spoken_dialogue.text: stand fast in this liberty wherewith ye have been made free,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma

spoken_dialogue.text: trust no one to be your teacher nor your minister, except he be a man of God, walking in his ways and keeping his commandments.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Bondage and liberty include the passage's stated spiritual meaning; do not literalize the bonds of iniquity.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting literal chains as the bonds of iniquity.

title: Alma teaches love and peace
summary: Alma teaches that each should love their neighbor and that there should be no contention. As high priest and founder of their church, he consecrates just men as priests and teachers, who watch over and nourish the people in righteousness.

explicit_facts.text: Alma teaches that every person should love their neighbor as themselves and that there should be no contention.
Alma is their high priest and the founder of their church.
Alma consecrates their priests and teachers; only just men are consecrated.
The priests and teachers watch over the people and nourish them with things pertaining to righteousness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma teaches the people; priests and teachers are present as a group.
unspecified_visual_details: The manner or setting of consecration.
The specific acts of watching over and teaching.

spoken_dialogue.text: every man should love his neighbor as himself,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The text does not provide individual names for the priests and teachers.
prohibited_inventions: Inventing names, biographies, or specific ceremonies for the priests and teachers.

title: The city of Helam
summary: The people prosper in the land they call Helam, multiply, and build a city they call the city of Helam.

explicit_facts.text: The people prosper exceedingly in the land and name it Helam.
They multiply and prosper in Helam and build a city named the city of Helam.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A settlement has developed into a city.
unspecified_visual_details: The city's architecture, size, and layout.

narration.text: they built a city, which they called the city of Helam.

prohibited_inventions: Inventing particular city structures or a founding ceremony.

title: A teaching of trust
summary: The account teaches that the Lord chastens his people and tries their patience and faith; those who trust in him will be lifted up at the last day, as was this people.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord sees fit to chasten his people and tries their patience and faith.
Those who put their trust in the Lord will be lifted up at the last day; the account says this was so with this people.

unspecified_visual_details: No present visual event or specific people are described in these verses.

narration.text: whosoever putteth his trust in him the same shall be lifted up at the last day.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a teaching and summary, not a narrated visible heavenly event.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting a divine appearance or the people being lifted into heaven.

title: A promise of deliverance
summary: The account says the people will be brought into bondage and that only the Lord can deliver them. The Lord delivers them and shows his mighty power, and they rejoice greatly.

explicit_facts.text: The account says the people were brought into bondage and none could deliver them but the Lord their God.
The Lord delivers them and shows his mighty power; the people rejoice greatly.

unspecified_visual_details: When and where this deliverance occurs in the chapter's chronology.
The means of bondage and deliverance.
Any visible form of the Lord.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses foreshadow or summarize bondage and deliverance; they do not specify the events or show a particular miracle.
prohibited_inventions: Inventing the bondage event, its timing, or a visible supernatural manifestation.

title: The Lamanite army appears
summary: While Alma's people till the land around the city of Helam, a Lamanite army appears at the borders. Alma's brethren flee their fields and gather in the city, frightened by the Lamanites' appearance.

explicit_facts.text: An army of the Lamanites is at the borders while the people are tilling land around Helam city.
Alma's brethren flee their fields and gather in the city, greatly frightened by the Lamanites' appearance.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lamanite army is visible at the border, and people gather in the city.
unspecified_visual_details: The army's size, weapons, clothing, and exact distance from the city.
The layout of the fields and city.

narration.text: an army of the Lamanites was in the borders of the land.

prohibited_inventions: Depicting an attack or combat; neither is described here.

title: Alma exhorts the people
summary: Alma stands among the gathered people and urges them not to fear, but to remember the Lord, who will deliver them. They quiet their fears and pray that the Lamanites will spare them, their wives, and their children.

explicit_facts.text: Alma stands among the people and exhorts them not to fear, but to remember the Lord their God, who will deliver them.
The people hush their fears and cry to the Lord to soften the Lamanites' hearts and spare them, their wives, and children.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma speaks to the gathered people; they pray.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact form of their prayer and their gestures.

spoken_dialogue.text: they should not be frightened, but that they should remember the Lord their God and he would deliver them.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The prayer is reported, not quoted verbatim.
prohibited_inventions: Inventing additional spoken words for Alma or the people.

title: Alma's people surrender
summary: The Lord softens the Lamanites' hearts. Alma and his brethren go forth and surrender to them, and the Lamanites take possession of Helam.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord softens the Lamanites' hearts.
Alma and his brethren go forth and deliver themselves into the Lamanites' hands; the Lamanites take possession of Helam.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma's people visibly surrender to the Lamanite army.
unspecified_visual_details: The Lamanites' appearance and manner of taking possession.

narration.text: Alma and his brethren went forth and delivered themselves up into their hands;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord's action is stated, but no visible appearance or particular mechanism is described.
prohibited_inventions: Showing a visible Lord or an attack.

title: The lost army finds Amulon's group
summary: The Lamanite army that followed Limhi's people has been lost in the wilderness for many days. It finds Noah's priests at Amulon, where they have begun to possess the land and till the ground. Amulon leads the priests.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanite armies that followed king Limhi's people have been lost in the wilderness for many days.
They find Noah's priests in Amulon; the priests have begun to possess the land and till the ground.
Amulon is the leader of the priests.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The priests are present where the Lamanite army finds them.
unspecified_visual_details: The duration and route of the army's journey beyond 'many days'.
The appearance of the place and the people.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The army's lost journey is reported; do not depict it as a separate present-tense scene here.
prohibited_inventions: Inventing a confrontation or dialogue at the meeting.

title: Amulon pleads for his people
summary: Amulon pleads with the Lamanites, and sends the wives, daughters of the Lamanites, to plead with their brethren not to destroy their husbands. The Lamanites have compassion and spare Amulon and his brethren.

explicit_facts.text: Amulon pleads with the Lamanites and sends the wives, who are daughters of the Lamanites, to plead with their brethren not to destroy their husbands.
The Lamanites have compassion on Amulon and his brethren and do not destroy them because of their wives.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Amulon and the wives plead before the Lamanites.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact words spoken and the physical arrangement of the plea.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The plea is summarized; no direct speech is supplied.
prohibited_inventions: Inventing dialogue or showing an execution.

title: Amulon's group joins the Lamanites
summary: Amulon and his brethren join the Lamanites, who are traveling in the wilderness in search of the land of Nephi. They discover Helam, where Alma and his brethren live. The Lamanites promise Alma's people their lives and liberty if they show the way to Nephi.

explicit_facts.text: Amulon and his brethren join the Lamanites; together they travel in the wilderness seeking the land of Nephi and discover Helam, occupied by Alma and his brethren.
The Lamanites promise Alma and his brethren their lives and liberty if they show the way to the land of Nephi.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lamanites and Amulon's group are together when they discover Helam.
unspecified_visual_details: The route, duration, and appearance of the journey.
Whether Alma's people are present when the promise is made.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses report the travel and promise; they do not provide the promise's exact spoken wording.
prohibited_inventions: Inventing dialogue or merging this journey with the earlier army's search for Limhi's people.

title: The Lamanites guard Helam
summary: After Alma shows the way to Nephi, the Lamanites break their promise and set guards around Helam over Alma and his brethren. The rest go to Nephi; some return to Helam with the wives and children of the guards left there.
characters: Wives and children of the Lamanite guards

explicit_facts.text: After Alma shows the way to Nephi, the Lamanites do not keep their promise and set guards around Helam over Alma and his brethren.
The remainder go to Nephi; some return to Helam with the wives and children of the guards left there.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lamanite guards are stationed around Helam; wives and children arrive with some returning Lamanites.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise timing and route of the groups' movements.
The number of guards, wives, and children.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are distinct movements: the guards remain at Helam, others go to Nephi, and some return with families.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting violence or inventing the guards' identities and motives.

title: Amulon appointed ruler
summary: The Lamanite king grants Amulon authority as king and ruler over his people in Helam, but limits him to the Lamanite king's will.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanite king grants Amulon the position of king and ruler over his people in Helam, with no power to act contrary to the Lamanite king's will.

unspecified_visual_details: The Lamanite king's appearance and location during the grant.
Whether the appointment is performed in a ceremony.

narration.text: he should have no power to do anything contrary to the will of the king of the Lamanites.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The grant is reported; the verse does not state that the Lamanite king is physically present in Helam.
prohibited_inventions: Showing the Lamanite king in Helam or inventing a coronation.
